He distinguished himself in the Battle of Dabhoi (1731) and the Battle of Bundelkhand (1732), contributing to the expansion of Maratha influence northward.[3] His most celebrated achievement, however, was the campaign against the Portuguese in the Konkan region, culminating in the decisive capture of the Vasai Fort on 16 May 1739.[4] The victory at Vasai ended more than two centuries of Portuguese dominance north of Goa and marked a turning point in Maratha control of the western coast of India..
